subject: Proposal: Renewal + Upsell — conditional price hold & accelerator credits

Subject: Proposal: Renewal + Upsell — conditional price hold & accelerator credits

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the deep product session last week — great feedback from your ML team. As we discussed, I pulled together a short proposal that aims to: (1) lock a price floor for the renewal term, (2) convert the current retainer into a committed baseline with a flexible uplift path, and (3) include accelerator credits tied to adoption (risk-share).

High-level (summary attached, see NR-Renewal-term-sheet-v1.pdf):
- Option A (12 months): convert $X/month retainer -> firm commit 6M tokens/month; 10% price hold for first 6 months; conditional accelerator credits up to 12% if usage growth > 40% vs baseline.
- Option B (24 months): deeper discount (15%) + 12 months price hold + staged true-up schedule.
- Risk-share: if NovaRetail exceeds the committed tier by >30% during months 4–12, we apply refundable credits to future invoices or a one-time invoice credit.

I attached a simple model so Procurement can see net effective rates and worst-case scenarios (pricing_model_spreadsheet.xlsx). If helpful, we can map these terms into a short amendment and route via DocuSign.

Quick asks:
1) Which option would Procurement prefer (12 vs 24 months)?
2) Do you need SLA additions for latency/availability in the amendment?

Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow to walk through the sheet.

Best,
Karthik

Hi Emily — quick follow up with the staged-commit numbers included. See attached pricing_model_spreadsheet.xlsx (tab: staged_commit).

Staged-commit illustrative (we can formalize milestones):
- Months 1–6: baseline commit = 4M tokens/month (convert existing retainer).
- Months 7–12: ramp to 8M tokens/month (step increase if adoption metric A > 15% MoM for 2 consecutive months).

Terming & credits: 
- Price hold: locked commercial rate for the first 12 months if you sign the 12-month amendment.
- Risk-share accelerator: up to 15% of month invoice can be issued as a refundable credit (applied to next invoice) if monthly usage growth > target. Credits are capped and expire after 9 months.
- True-up: quarterly true-up with invoice adjustments; overage capped at 125% of committed rate pricing until a new tier is signed.

If Procurement wants stronger protections we can:
- Add SLA credit language for sustained latency > 250ms (discussed below), or
- Convert a portion of credits to an escrow instrument that only releases on successful ramp milestones.

If you give me the preferred ramp schedule I’ll produce a redline-ready amendment and send to Legal.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Emily — Monica on CS here. Quick operational notes from our side that matter for the ramp and commitment: 

- Ramp milestones we recommend: 4 weeks (ingestion & integration), 10 weeks (full model calls at 50% baseline), 18 weeks (production at target).
- Dedicated pool recommendation: given your traffic profile, a small Dedicated instance for first 12 weeks reduces tail latency and makes the SLA guarantees easier to meet.
- Instrumentation: we will provide a shared dashboard for token-level cost tracking and weekly spike alerts.

If you’d like, we can run a short canary (3 customers, 2 weeks) to validate performance prior to committing to the larger tier. That helps minimize risk for NovaRetail and makes the accelerator credit handshake easier.

—Monica

Emily — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the POC pdf. Per alignment with Legal and CS, summary of what Redwood can commit to in an amendment (I will send a redline + DocuSign link tomorrow):

- Term: 12 months (price hold limited to months 1–12 as requested).
- Commit: staged commit starting at 4M tokens/month, ramp to 8M/month on agreed milestones (6-week and 12-week checkpoints).
- Credits: accelerator credits up to 15% of invoice value, applied to future invoices only (no cash refunds). Credits expire after 9 months if unused.
- SLA: p95 latency credit trigger at sustained > 250ms for 2 consecutive days; credit formula to mirror standard Redwood SLA (we'll surface specific % in the amendment).
- Audit logs: 13 months retention — confirmed.
- Escrow option: we can convert up to 30% of accelerator credits to an escrow release tied to ramp milestones if you want stronger assurance.

Attached: NR-Renewal-term-sheet-v2.docx (amendment draft will reflect these bullets). HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DL-2026-0117.
